lens: A quieter news cycle turned the spotlight onto deals already in motion: argenx commenced its tender offer for Forte Biosciences (Guggenheim, Goldman), and the full Prologis/SEGRO Rule 2.7 filing revealed a seven covered-bank roster across both sides — even as LivePerson’s debt-laden sale to SoundHound headed for an Aug 20 vote and stocks slipped from record territory.

stories.headline: argenx commences its tender offer for Forte Biosciences; Guggenheim advises Forte, Goldman advises argenx
stories.why_it_matters: argenx (via Avena Merger Sub) has formally COMMENCED its all-cash tender offer for all shares of Forte Biosciences (Nasdaq: FBRX), and Forte’s board filed its SC 14D-9 recommending shareholders tender — advancing the ~$2.2B acquisition first announced Jul 27 to a live, filed tender stage. The SC 14D-9 names Guggenheim Securities as Forte’s financial adviser (fairness opinion) and Goldman Sachs as argenx’s adviser. A commenced tender runs a compressed diligence-and-close clock to the offer expiration.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Guggenheim (Forte) and Goldman (argenx) — a commenced tender offer runs a tight confirmatory-diligence and close timeline a secure room keeps organized through expiration.

deal_clock.event: argenx agrees to acquire Forte Biosciences (~$2.2B)
Tender offer commenced; Forte files SC 14D-9 recommending tender

stories.headline: Prologis’ ~$18.8B recommended combination with SEGRO names a seven covered-bank roster across both sides
stories.why_it_matters: The full Rule 2.7 announcement for Prologis’ ~£14.0B (~$18.8B) recommended all-share combination with UK logistics REIT SEGRO names advisers on BOTH sides — and seven are covered banks. SEGRO (sell-side) is advised by Evercore and Morgan Stanley (joint lead financial advisers), with Goldman Sachs also advising and UBS as corporate broker/financial adviser; Prologis (buy-side) is advised by J.P. Morgan (joint lead, with Eastdil), BofA Securities and Citi (with Rothschild). A cross-border public-company REIT combination runs UK Takeover Code, antitrust and shareholder-documentation workstreams to a targeted 1H 2027 close.
stories.suggested_action: This deal touches seven covered desks at once — engage the SEGRO advisers (Evercore, Morgan Stanley, Goldman, UBS) and the Prologis advisers (JPMorgan, BofA, Citi). A ~$18.8B cross-border REIT combination runs months of Takeover Code and antitrust diligence a secure room organizes.

stories.headline: LivePerson heads to an Aug 20 vote on its stock-for-stock sale to SoundHound AI; Houlihan Lokey advises LivePerson
stories.why_it_matters: LivePerson (Nasdaq: LPSN) filed further solicitation material (Form 425) ahead of its Aug 20 special meeting on its stock-for-stock merger with SoundHound AI (Nasdaq: SOUN), first announced Apr 21. Houlihan Lokey Capital is LivePerson’s financial adviser and delivered the fairness opinion. The structure is unusual — secured noteholders agreed to exchange ~$350M of par notes at a discount to enable common-stock consideration — so the vote carries real execution risk. A contested-feeling shareholder vote runs heavy proxy-solicitation and disclosure workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Houlihan Lokey (LivePerson) — a debt-laden stock-for-stock merger heading to a knife-edge shareholder vote runs intensive proxy and disclosure workstreams a secure room supports through the Aug 20 meeting.

deal_clock.event: SoundHound AI agrees to acquire LivePerson (stock-for-stock)

stories.headline: Quantum-computing firm Pasqal files its definitive de-SPAC proxy with Bleichroeder; Lazard and Jefferies advise
stories.why_it_matters: Pasqal, a French quantum-computing company, filed a definitive proxy (DEFM14A) for its business combination with Bleichroeder Acquisition Corp. II (Nasdaq: BBCQ), setting the shareholder vote to take the company public. The filing names Lazard as financial adviser to the Pasqal board and Jefferies as lead placement agent on the associated PIPE/convertible financing. A de-SPAC with a concurrent private financing runs parallel proxy, PIPE and disclosure workstreams.
stories.suggested_action: Note Lazard (Pasqal board) and Jefferies (placement agent) — a de-SPAC with a concurrent PIPE runs parallel proxy and private-financing diligence a secure room organizes into the vote.

stories.headline: BofA (lead) and RBC advise Gran Tierra on its $1.33B sale of its Colombia/Ecuador business to Maurel & Prom
stories.why_it_matters: Still fresh from Aug 5: Gran Tierra Energy (NYSE/TSX: GTE) agreed to sell its Colombia and Ecuador business — all of its South American assets — to Maurel & Prom (a Pertamina subsidiary) for $1.33B total consideration (~$315M net cash proceeds). BofA Securities is lead financial adviser (and fairness-opinion provider) to Gran Tierra, with RBC Capital Markets also advising (sell-side). A cross-border upstream divestiture runs reserve, regulatory and confirmatory diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage BofA and RBC (Gran Tierra) — a $1.33B cross-border upstream divestiture runs reserve, regulatory and confirmatory diligence a data room supports.

deal_clock.event: Gran Tierra agrees to sell Colombia/Ecuador business ($1.33B)

stories.headline: Morgan Stanley advises gChem and Piper Sandler advises ContextLogic on the $850M specialty-chemicals acquisition
stories.why_it_matters: Still fresh from Aug 5: ContextLogic (Nasdaq: LOGC) agreed to acquire gChem — a specialty-chemicals maker (DMSO for pharma, semiconductors, ag and aerospace), sold by EagleTree Capital — for $850M enterprise value. Morgan Stanley is exclusive financial adviser to gChem (sell-side) and Piper Sandler advises ContextLogic (buy-side). A sponsor-exit chemicals carve-out runs environmental, contract and QofE diligence to close.
stories.suggested_action: Engage Morgan Stanley (gChem) and Piper Sandler (ContextLogic) — an $850M specialty-chemicals sale runs environmental and quality-of-earnings diligence a secure room keeps organized.

stories.headline: Stocks slip from record territory — S&P -0.17%, Nasdaq -0.83% — as megacap tech cools and the 10Y firms to ~4.65%
stories.why_it_matters: After the early-August run to records, equities pulled back: the S&P 500 eased -0.17% (~7,724) and the Nasdaq fell -0.83% (~26,363) as megacap tech gave back gains, while the Dow held +0.49% (~54,349) on defensives. The VIX firmed to ~16.0 and the 10Y Treasury ticked up to ~4.65%. Advisory names were mixed (GS +0.7%, JPM +0.5%, JEF +0.9%, EVR -0.3%) as the deal calendar stayed active on cross-border and healthcare processes. A modest risk-off day doesn’t slow signed processes — it sharpens the focus on execution certainty.
stories.suggested_action: Use the pullback to keep the conversation on execution, not sentiment — signed processes need to stay on timeline regardless of the tape, and room readiness protects that.

A slow news day is exactly when live processes need to stay on timeline — that’s a room-readiness conversation. How are the mandates you’re carrying tracking to their close dates?

items.company: GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) — Patient Care Solutions
items.lead: On its Q2 call, CEO Peter Arduini confirmed a formal review of strategic options for the Patient Care Solutions segment, explicitly including “a sale and other value-enhancing transactions.” Segment Q2 revenue was $675M, down 13.3%.
items.why_unverified: Company-confirmed that a review is underway — but whether it sells, at what price, to whom, with which adviser, and on what timeline are all unconfirmed. A potential carve-out mandate, not a rumored deal.
